summary: Console live filter application becomes slow and intermittently strips tracehook params on large orgs
description: Issue summary: Customer AtlasHealth reports that when applying complex live filters on their org-scoped dashboards (high cardinality routes + long time ranges), the console UI becomes slow (>8s to apply) and in ~30% of attempts the tracehook parameters in alert links and exported rows are missing or truncated. Impact: alerts linked from dashboard heatmaps resolve to 404s for engineers; scheduled CSV exports are missing tracehook columns causing investigation churn. This started for AtlasHealth on 2026-03-09 after a retention compaction roll and appears to affect other large customers sporadically.
impact: Customer-facing dashboards and alert links broken, scheduled exports missing tracehook context, SRE and support escalations required for every major spike
steps_to_reproduce: Login as a large org admin (org with >100k unique route tags)
Open Console > Dashboards > select heatmap with route filter and time range of 72h
Apply a compound live filter: route in (high-cardinality set) AND status != 200 AND tag_exists(trace_id)
Wait for UI to apply filter; observe UI latency and check alert drilldown links for tracehook parameters
Export scheduled CSV for same panel and inspect tracehook_token and trace_id columns
expected_behavior: Filters apply under 2s for typical dashboards; tracehook params are preserved on drilldown links and CSV exports
actual_behavior: Filter application stalls 6-12s; in ~30% of runs the tracehook query params are missing or truncated in drilldown URLs and exported CSV cells
logs: console-frontend logs (2026-03-10T15:12:04Z): WARN request-slow-apply time_ms=8123 route_count=123456 filter_expr=...
api-gateway (2026-03-10T15:12:05Z): WARN downstream-timeout-yellow request_id=req_9f8b tracehook-strip=true upstream=usage-ingest cluster=us-east
usage-ingest (2026-03-10T15:12:06Z): ERROR export-sanitizer removed_param=tracehook_token reason=prefix-eviction retention_bucket=hot_to_cold
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 16:00 - Support: Confirmed reproducible with AtlasHealth account. Issue frequency ~3/10 attempts during peak query times.
2026-03-10 17:10 - SRE: Correlated slow filter applies with high prefix cache evictions on serving-runtime (KV cache churn). See grafana dashboard 'prefix-cache/evictions-us-east'.
2026-03-10 18:00 - Infra: Noted a retention compaction job for usage-exports ran 2026-03-09 23:30 which increased index shard merges and temporarily elevated ingest latency.

Hypothesis 1: When frontend retries or request is proxied under load, an intermediate sanitizer service performs defensive parameter pruning for long query strings. Pruning logic considers route cardinality and will drop query params if size threshold exceeded. This logic mistakenly matched tracehook token param names when URL rewriting occurred during retry.
Hypothesis 2: CSV export path goes through export-sanitizer (usage-ingest); a race between compaction-driven eviction and export-sanitizer's parameter whitelist causes intermittent missing columns.
Related signals: spike in 429s to export-sanitizer (2026-03-09T23:30 to 2026-03-10T02:00), console-frontend slow apply correlates with those windows.
Linked to support ticket SUP-712345 (large-org export slowdowns) and internal INT-223 (export-sanitizer rate limiting change rolled 2026-03-09).
customer_communication: 2026-03-10 16:05 - Support -> AtlasHealth: Acknowledged report and requested example dashboard + time window. Asked for confirmation of org_id and a reproducible URL.
2026-03-10 17:20 - AtlasHealth: Provided dashboard id db_78a, sample route list, and CSV export with missing tracehook columns attached.
2026-03-11 09:00 - Support: Notified customer that engineering is investigating and provided a temporary mitigation (narrow time range / split filters to reduce cardinality).
actions_taken: Rolled back export-sanitizer throttle change from INT-223 as a temporary mitigation (2026-03-10 19:12)
Added defensive logging to console-frontend to capture full outgoing drilldown URLs and parameter length (2026-03-10 20:00) - PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4210
Whitelisted tracehook_token & trace_id in export-sanitizer to avoid param pruning during retry (temporary hotfix)
next_steps: SRE: Run controlled load test against export-sanitizer to validate whitelist fixes and ensure no CSV leakage (due 2026-03-13)
Engineering: Implement robust param-preservation in the proxy layer and add unit tests for high-cardinality filter flows (owner: Liam O'Connor, due 2026-03-19)
Product/Support: Create short KB article for large orgs documenting recommended filter patterns and the temporary mitigation steps
Postmortem: If fix confirmed, schedule postmortem and customer-facing incident summary page on status.redwood.ai
resolution: Partial mitigation deployed: export-sanitizer whitelist and rollback of throttle change reduced occurrences from ~30% to <2% for AtlasHealth. Root cause appears to be combined effect of retention compaction-induced ingest pressure and an over-aggressive parameter-pruning change (INT-223). Full fix requires proxy logic change and additional unit tests. Customer informed and given mitigation steps.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-11 14:30 - Hotfix deployed to export-sanitizer and rolling restarts completed in us-east. Monitoring shows reduced error rate.
2026-03-12 10:00 - Engineering: Began work on proxy param-preservation refactor. Linked PR created for review.
Follow-up tasks: INT ticket for permanent fix INT-421 (proxy-preserve-params), scheduled postmortem and KB article creation
